newsitem.title: USA: Dole cuts Clinton lead in Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Dole cuts Clinton lead in Reuters poll.

text.p: By Alan Elsner, U.S. Political Correspondent
Republican Bob Dole cut President Bill Clinton's lead to 7.7 percentage points in the Reuters daily tracking poll released on Thursday.

Clinton led with 41.9 percent, ahead of Dole's 34.2 percent. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot scored 8.6 percent and 13.4 percent said they were still undecided with only five days to go before the election.

The poll, conducted by John Zogby Group International, surveyed approximately 1,200 likely voters over a three-day period, creating a new three-day rolling average each day. The latest results involved the average of Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday polling. The margin of sampling error was plus or minus 3 percent.

Pollster John Zogby said in Wednesday's polling alone, Clinton's lead was down to five percentage points. Dole had been making up ground consistently in the past few days, although his support was still stuck below 35 percent.
Clinton's support was at its lowest level since the daily poll began on Oct. 1.

"Clinton's numbers continue to decline while Dole has inched up a little bit. In addition to Clinton's decline, the real dynamics here continue to be Perot's increase, edging closer to double-digits," Zogby said.
Perot has stressed the issue of campaign finance reform while Clinton has been embarrassed by the disclosure that the Democratic Party raised large sums from Asian businessmen.
The race for Congress remained tight with 39.7 percent saying they would vote for the Democrat in their local district and 38.2 percent voicing support for the Republican.
Asked which party they would prefer to see controlling the Congress, however, voters opted for the Republicans by 5.5 percent in the Senate and by 3.7 percent in the House of Representatives.

In another sign that Republicans seem to be making a last-minute recovery, House Speaker Newt Gingrich's positive job rating has risen five points in the past four days to 30.9 percent, although 60.4 percent still view him negatively.
